line: Crowley’s Five of Swords: Defeat, Geburah producing disruption, Venus ruling Aquarius.

sections.title: What Crowley names
sections.line: The chapter name for the card. The second quotation gives the element of its suit.

quotes.quote: The Five of Swords is similarly troublesome; the card is called Defeat.
“Wands”, attributed to Fire; “Cups”, to Water; “Swords”, to Air;

sections.title: Its place on the Tree and in the zodiac
sections.line: The chapter opens with Geburah, and gives Venus as ruling Aquarius.

quotes.quote: as Venus here rules Aquarius, weakness

sections.title: What it figures
sections.line: Crowley reads the intellect as enfeebled by sentiment, and the hilts as an inverted pentagram.

quotes.quote: The intellect has been enfeebled by sentiment.
The hilts of the swords form the inverted pentagram, always a symbol of somewhat sinister tendency.
